terms.definition: The original figure before a transformation.
The resulting figure after a transformation.
A mapping that sends each point of a figure to an image point.
A transformation that moves every point the same distance in the same direction.
An ordered horizontal and vertical displacement used to describe a translation.
A transformation that maps points across a line so the line is the perpendicular bisector of each point-image segment.
The mirror line used in a reflection.
A transformation that turns a figure through a specified angle about a fixed center.
The fixed point about which a rotation occurs.
The amount and direction through which a figure turns.
A sequence of two or more transformations applied in a specified order.
A transformation that preserves distance and angle measure.
A distance-preserving transformation; in plane geometry, translations, reflections and rotations are isometries.
A property or quantity that remains unchanged under a transformation.
Figures with the same size and shape that can be mapped onto one another by rigid motions.
Points in a preimage and image that are paired by a transformation or congruence mapping.
The clockwise or counterclockwise order of vertices around a figure.
Symmetry in which reflection across a line maps a figure onto itself.
Symmetry in which a rotation less than 360 degrees maps a figure onto itself.
The number of times a figure maps onto itself during one full 360-degree rotation.
Symmetry under a 180-degree rotation about a center point.
A covering of the plane by repeated figures with no gaps or overlaps.
A repeating strip pattern generated by translations and possibly other symmetries.
A smallest repeating portion that can generate a larger transformation-based pattern.
